preheader: 61 books reviewed in the British papers this week, fiction and non-fiction, one line each.

books.book: Yakuza: A 400-Year History of the Japanese Underworld
books.author: Andrew Rankin
books.subject: True crime
books.line: Four centuries of Japan's organised crime gangs, from their origins to their present decline.
books.why: A secret world with its own codes, rituals and four hundred years of stories.

books.book: Blood on the Thames: Murder, Money and the Making of the Modern Detective
books.author: Thomas Morris
books.subject: True crime
books.line: Murder and money on the Thames, and how they helped make the modern detective.
books.why: Murder on the Thames at the birth of detective work: a ready-made period crime world.

books.author: Daria Santini
books.subject: Espionage
books.line: The life of Edith Tudor Hart, emigre, photographer and secret agent.
books.why: A photographer leading a double life as a secret agent, with a striking woman at the centre.

books.author: Marina Litvinenko
books.subject: Biography & memoir
books.line: Twenty years after her husband's murder, Marina Litvinenko reflects on love and resilience.
books.why: The widow's own account of one of the most notorious state killings of the century.

books.author: Chris Hedges and Joe Sacco
books.subject: Politics & world affairs

books.author: Laura Kuenssberg
books.subject: Politics & world affairs
books.line: After two decades of studied neutrality, the BBC journalist sets out what she thinks is wrong with modern politics.

books.book: The Rise of Reform: The Inside Story of Britain's Political Disruptors
